shots.title: Vienna from above
shots.kicker: Aerial · city scale · outline © OpenStreetMap contributors
shots.idea: Open on the whole city seen from above. A heat map builds up district by district and shows where Vienna overheats in summer. The camera settles on the dense inner west around Westbahnhof, our case study.

shots.title: Westbahnhof: the district and its border
shots.idea: A wider view of the area around Westbahnhof: every building stands alike, the district and its surroundings. Then the buildings around it fade back, and the district used in all the following shots stands out. The place and its current state, before anything is added.

shots.title: Raumpark: a second city, one level up
shots.kicker: Isometric · the city's volumes taken up one level
shots.idea: City design is also climate design, and vice versa. RAUMPARK stands for a new typology of cities in the era of the New Climatic Regime: urban expansions and densifications in the form of populated green spaces and forests above, and interlinked with, the existing city. The shot shows it with the city's own material: some blocks of the existing city take the colours of the uses (culture, health & wellbeing, residential, green areas). The pylons rise from the street crossings with green climbing them, and the deck spreads out along the streets. Then the coloured blocks' volumes are duplicated, lift off and deform into the volumes on the deck, mostly running in one direction: what the city has, taken up one level and reshaped to fit.
shots.camera: Fixed isometric, the view of the following shots; the Raumpark grows out of the district
shots.graphics: Blocks in use colours · pylons with climbing green · deck · duplicated volumes morphing onto the deck
shots.data: Raumpark concept: pylon positions, deck outline, programme (from the research team)

shots.title: Westbahnhof: sun & shade, summer and winter
shots.idea: Same view, the Raumpark now in place above the district. Two days run as time-lapses: 21 June, with the sun high on a long arc and a short shadow under the deck, then 21 December, with the sun low on a short arc and the deck's shadow stretching far across streets and courtyards. Both day arcs stay visible, so the difference reads at once.
shots.camera: Fixed isometric · time-lapse 21 June, then 21 December
shots.graphics: Summer and winter sun arcs · deck shadow
shots.data: Sun position for Vienna on 21 June and 21 December (calculated) · 3D model of the area

shots.title: Westbahnhof: heat without / with Raumpark
shots.idea: Same view of the district, now as heat. First without the Raumpark: the paved streets and the station forecourt glow warm red, the courtyards are milder. Then the Raumpark fades in and the heat map shifts: under and around the deck the ground turns cooler blue. Same view, same scale, so the difference reads at a glance.
shots.camera: Fixed isometric; without → Raumpark fades in → with
shots.graphics: Blue → red heat map · semi-transparent deck
shots.data: Surface temperature or heat-stress simulation with and without the deck (to confirm)

shots.title: Westbahnhof: wind
shots.idea: Same camera, new layer: wind particles run through the streets and over the deck. Channelled jets and sheltered corners become visible, and the deck level turns out windier than the street.
shots.camera: Same isometric view, gentle push-in to street level
shots.data: CFD results or schematic flow (to decide)
shots.transition: Same camera, the model comes apart

shots.title: Layers
shots.kicker: Exploded axo · city scale to deck
shots.idea: After the district's sun, heat and wind, the same model comes apart into its layers: the existing city stays on the ground, then the pylons over the street crossings, the deck that branches along the streets and the use volumes on top lift away one after the other, thin lines marking where the pylons land. Then the stack closes again and the camera goes down to one window.
shots.camera: Isometric, the stack opens at one layer after the other
shots.graphics: Exploded layers · lines where the pylons land
shots.data: 3D model of the district, split into layers
shots.transition: Back together, push in on a window

shots.title: Window & model, side by side
shots.idea: Starts on the overview of the district with the Raumpark. The deck turns transparent and the camera pushes in on one window of a Gründerzeit house below it. Then the view out of that window fills the screen, with light and shade moving through the room over the day, while a small isometric sun study in the corner shows the same moment with the window marked. Both run in sync, so the abstract model meets everyday experience.
shots.camera: Overview → deck fades to transparent → push-in on one window → full-screen window view with a synced model inset
shots.graphics: Transparent deck · window highlight · model inset · shared clock
shots.data: Same sun data · one reference flat / window

shots.title: Quality of sunlight
shots.kicker: Isometric · sun hours over 20 March, in one picture
shots.idea: How much sun reaches the people who live here, below the Raumpark and on it. The whole of 20 March, the equinox and the usual day for daylight studies, merged into one picture: the streets, courtyards, roofs and the deck show how many hours of direct sun they get over the day, from sky blue (little) to light orange (sun all day). The shadows of the existing blocks, the deck and its volumes are all in it, so the shot shows where the new level keeps light for the city below and where it gains the best light on top. The day's sun arc runs above, with its times.
shots.camera: Same isometric view, still; the camera drifts in slowly
shots.graphics: Sun hours on ground, roofs and deck · the day's sun arc with times · scale
shots.data: Sun position for Vienna on 20 March (calculated) · 3D model of the area and the Raumpark
shots.transition: Same camera, from light to energy

shots.title: Greenery & solar income
shots.kicker: Diagram · heat map on the deck
shots.idea: A diagram over the whole deck: a heat map of how much sun each part receives over the year, with the use volumes casting their shade. From it follows where planting thrives, where shade-loving planting belongs, and where PV pays off, with the share of each shown as bars.
shots.camera: Top-down / isometric diagram, heat map sweeps in
shots.graphics: Solar heat map · legend · share bars · PV · PV on the sloped, sun-facing sides of the volumes
shots.data: Yearly sun on the deck (calculated) · planting and PV assumptions
